updates.name: Kristen Veum
updates.bio: Research soil scientist with USDA-ARS in Columbia, Missouri, whose cross-disciplinary work centers on assessing soil health in cropping systems and how land use and management shape it. She leads work on a continental-scale soil health scoring framework, helped build the SHAPE assessment tool, and evaluates new indicators and which conservation practices improve soil health.
updates.research_interests: soil health assessment; soil health indicators and scoring (SHAPE); cropping systems and conservation management effects on soil; large-scale soil health data aggregation and analysis
updates.current_affiliation: USDA-ARS Cropping Systems and Water Quality Research Unit, Columbia, Missouri
updates.evidence: Leader(s) Ken Sudduth (RL), Claire Baffaut (Lead), Lori Abendroth, Newell Kitchen, Adam Schreiner-McGraw, Kristen Veum
updates.notes: ARS profile (200) states her role and research. Same text also on darec.missouri.edu/dr-kristen-veum (200), which links the ARS profile. ORCID 0000-0002-6492-913X (pub.orcid.org name Kristen Veum) lists no employment and no fetched official page links it, so not recorded. No Google Scholar link on either profile. Verifier: evidence replaced with the verbatim CMRB page text; bio no longer equates SHAPE with the continental scoring system, which the page describes separately.

updates.name: Daniel R. LeCain
updates.bio: Plant physiologist with the USDA Agricultural Research Service. A photo caption in a 2007 agency release names LeCain and Jack Morgan as using open-top chambers to expose native rangeland plants to doubled carbon dioxide on the Colorado shortgrass steppe; the study found the shrub fringed sage gained far more biomass than the grasses.
updates.evidence: Technicians Dan LeCain Plant Physiologist USDA-ARS
updates.notes: Only agency pages found: the archived 2007 ARS news release (photo caption names Plant physiologists Jack Morgan and Dan LeCain) and the ARS PHACE 'Who We Are' page, which lists him under Technicians (Plant Physiologist, USDA-ARS), not as a PHACE principal investigator; the work list's 'co-PI' role is not supported by that page. No fetched page states retirement, so status left null. ORCID 0000-0003-0977-8735 (pub.orcid.org name Daniel LeCain) lists no employment and is not linked from an official page, so not recorded. No ARS profile page found. Verifier: evidence replaced with the verbatim PHACE page text; bio now says the release credits him only in the photo caption (the article body does not name him).

updates.name: Jack A. Morgan
updates.bio: USDA-ARS plant physiologist who, per a 2011 agency release, led the Prairie Heating and CO2 Enrichment (PHACE) experiment run by the Rangeland Resources Research Unit near Cheyenne, Wyoming. Using CO2 pipelines and infrared heaters on native mixed-grass rangeland, the study found elevated CO2 offset warming-driven soil water loss, and only warm-season grasses grew more under combined CO2 and warming.
updates.evidence: ARS plant physiologist Jack Morgan leads the study
updates.notes: Archived 2011 ARS release (200). The archived 2007 ARS release (elevated-carbon-dioxide-spurs-shrub-growth) calls him 'Plant physiologist Jack A. Morgan, research leader of the ARS Rangeland Resources Research Unit in Fort Collins'. The ARS PHACE 'Who We Are' page lists him first among Principal Investigators. No fetched page states retirement or emeritus status, so status left null. No ARS profile page or ORCID tie found. Verifier: evidence bracket insertion removed so the quote is verbatim; bio corrected: the release attributes the warm-season grass boost to CO2 and warming together, not CO2 alone.

updates.name: Alex Harper
updates.bio: Deputy Director of the Central and Northern California Ocean Observing System (CeNCOOS) through Cal Poly Humboldt, and earlier its program manager at MBARI. A chemical oceanographer (Ph.D., Florida State) whose dissertation studied northern Gulf of Mexico mercury cycling, Harper was also a U.S. IOOS program analyst at NOAA and a California Sea Grant climate resilience specialist.
updates.research_interests: regional ocean observing systems; ocean acidification and hypoxia monitoring; integrating biological and ecosystem observations; mercury biogeochemistry
updates.evidence: Alex Harper, Program Staff, Deputy Director, CeNCOOS
updates.notes: Bio from the short CV CeNCOOS hosts (2024 upload, 200), which lists Deputy Director (2024) under Cal Poly Humboldt. CeNCOOS staff page (cencoos.org/about/staff/ redirects to organization-overview/staff-governing-council/) lists Harper as Deputy Director. No pronoun used: none of the fetched pages uses one for Harper. No ORCID or Google Scholar link found. Verifier: bio changed 'worked on U.S. IOOS planning' to the CV's stated position (Program Analyst, U.S. IOOS, NOAA).

updates.name: Kyle Derby
updates.bio: Research Coordinator at the Chesapeake Bay Maryland NERR. On a Delaware NERR podcast, Derby explains how talks he began with the Delaware and Virginia reserves grew into Tea Time, a system-wide study in which reserves buried standardized tea bags in marshes for about 90 days to compare belowground decomposition, a process tied to wetland carbon storage.
updates.current_affiliation: Chesapeake Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve (Maryland), Maryland Department of Natural Resources
updates.notes: Bio source is the Delaware NERR 'Skimmer Says' podcast episode page with transcript (200), in which he says he is the Research Coordinator for the Chesapeake Bay Maryland NERR and started in 2019. Existing ORCID 0009-0006-4131-7399 checked: pub.orcid.org name Robert Kyle Derby, employment Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Chesapeake Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve, Research Coordinator (from 2018). Existing homepage is the reserve home page, not a personal page; no individual profile found. A 2015 Garden Club of America scholarship page names an R. Kyle Derby (UMD master's, marsh methane) but nothing ties it to the reserve, so not used. Verifier: bio no longer says he alone started the project or gives a start year (podcast says he had just started in 2019; ORCID employment starts 2018); the podcast says the three reserves jointly pitched it to the system.

updates.name: Patricia Delgado
updates.bio: Superintendent and wetland ecologist at Jug Bay Wetlands Sanctuary in Maryland, with over 25 years of wetland research. At the sanctuary she promotes environmental education and stewardship, research, citizen science and communicating science to visitors. Her training includes a marine biology degree from Costa Rica's Universidad Nacional de Heredia and LSU graduate degrees in oceanography and coastal sciences.
updates.notes: Jug Bay 'Our People' page (200) is a staff page, so no homepage. Identity: Maryland DNR CBNERR contact page lists 'Jug Bay Wetlands Sanctuary Manager: Dr. Patricia Delgado', consistent. The page uses 'she' for her. No ORCID found tied to the sanctuary.

updates.name: Kiersten Stanzel
updates.bio: Executive Director of the Coastal Bend Bays & Estuaries Program since September 2022, after serving as its Director of Partnerships. She manages program business and operations, builds partnerships and funding, and works with the board. She holds a Ph.D. in marine science from UT Austin and was earlier a research associate with the Mission-Aransas NERR.
updates.notes: CBBEP staff page (200) carries a full bio paragraph; it is a staff list, so no homepage. The page uses 'she'. No ORCID record under her name found.
